title: Clamped rectangular cantilever first bending mode
purpose: Verify that the public modal Study assembles consistent solid stiffness and mass, eliminates fixed degrees of freedom, resolves low modes accurately, and returns mass-normalized mode fields with eigenpair residual evidence.
physics: Two-dimensional plane-stress linear-elastic cantilever free vibration

execution.command: python -m pytest -q tests/test_dynamics.py -k modal_step; mpiexec -n 2 python -m pytest -q tests/test_parallel_modal.py
execution.evidence: A Q2 plane-stress solid mesh with 8 by 2 cells gives a first bending frequency of 163.27832561 Hz, 2.60 percent below the Euler--Bernoulli value 167.63805088 Hz. Three eigenpairs pass a relative residual threshold of 1e-7 and the fixed dofs are absent from the reduced K--M problem.

observables: Relative SLEPc eigenpair residual for every accepted mode.
acceptance: The first finite-element bending frequency must remain within 3.5 percent of the Euler--Bernoulli slender-beam reference for the fixed Q2 mesh.
The first three accepted frequencies must be positive and strictly increasing.
Every relative eigenpair residual must remain below 1e-7.
The result must expose exactly three mode fields through the common SimulationResult contract.
The two-rank distributed solve must reproduce the serial frequencies within 1e-7 relative error.

quantities.name: first_natural_frequency
quantities.unit: Hz for the declared SI inputs
quantities.description: First SLEPc mode for a 1.0 by 0.2 plane-stress cantilever with E=210 GPa, nu=0.3 and density=7800 kg/m^3.

limitations: Euler--Bernoulli theory is used only as a bounded first-mode reference; the finite-height 2D solid contains shear and rotary effects absent from that theory.
This benchmark verifies undamped linear modes, not complex modes, harmonic response or nonlinear vibration.
The 3.5 percent criterion is an AgentFEM verification contract, not an external standard tolerance.
